newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to meet Egypt's Mubarak on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to meet Egypt's Mubarak on Friday.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will meet with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Friday to discuss the state of peace talks with Israel, a PLO official said on Tuesday.

Arafat's spokesman Nabil Abu Rdaineh said the Palestinian leader spoke to Mubarak by phone twice on Tuesday, informing him that no progress had been made in talks on a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.

"Despite all the efforts exerted to make progress on Hebron, there is still no achievement, therefore President Arafat has decided to hold talks with President Mubarak in Cairo on Friday morning," Abu Rdaineh told Reuters by phone from Vienna where Arafat is on an official visit.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators, who met on Monday for the first time in 10 days, have been struggling since September to seal terms of the long overdue Israeli withdrawal outlined in a peace agreement reached more than a year ago.

Hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected last May, has sought tighter security arrangements for 400 Jews living among 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron before ordering the withdrawal of Israeli troops from about 80 percent of the city.
Palestinians say Netanyahu is trying to renege on the peace deal signed by his Labour party predecessors.
The United States, sponsor of Arab-Israeli peace talks since they were launched in 1991, voiced increasing impatience on Tuesday with the slow pace of talks.
"It appears that the discussions on Hebron are not making the progress that we had all hoped they would make," Secretary of State Warren Christopher told reporters in Washington.
Egypt in 1979 was the first Arab state to sign a peace deal with Israel and has had a role in talks between Israel and the PLO since their breakthrough 1993 interim peace deal.
